question: What is the primary purpose of national professional nursing organizations?

options.A: To provide free medical treatment to rural communities
options.B: To unite practitioners, protect public health, and advance the profession
options.C: To manage hospital budgets and hire medical doctors
options.D: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for local clinics

explanation: These organizations exist to bring nurses together, safeguard the health of the public through high standards, and push the profession forward. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h1)

question: How do national nursing bodies connect individual clinicians to government decisions?

options.A: By providing a collective voice for policy influence
options.B: By directly writing laws without legislative approval
options.C: By collecting taxes from every registered nurse
options.D: By appointing government ministers of health

explanation: Instead of individual nurses trying to reach lawmakers alone, these bodies pool numbers and authority to influence health policies. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the main legal responsibility of the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria?

options.A: To regulate nursing education and protect the public
options.B: To provide financial loans for building private clinics
options.C: To negotiate better salaries and housing allowances for nurses
options.D: To supply medical equipment to public hospitals

explanation: The council is a regulatory body, meaning its main job is to set standards and protect the public, not to act as a salary-negotiating trade union. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following functions does the NMCN NOT perform?

options.A: Disciplining nurses who commit professional misconduct
options.B: Issuing practicing licenses to qualified practitioners
options.C: Accrediting nursing training institutions and programs
options.D: Negotiating annual salary increases with the government

explanation: Salary negotiations and welfare issues are handled by trade unions, whereas the NMCN focuses strictly on regulation, licensing, and discipline. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h2)

question: What primary function does NANNM perform for Nigerian nurses?

options.A: Registering student nurses at the start of training
options.B: Inspecting nursing schools for curriculum approval
options.C: Defending their socio-economic welfare and working conditions
options.D: Conducting professional board examinations and licensing

explanation: NANNM operates as a trade union, focusing on workers' rights, salaries, and workplace safety rather than board examinations. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why is it important to distinguish NANNM from the NMCN?

options.A: One is a trade union for welfare, while the other is a regulatory body for standards
options.B: One handles only male nurses, while the other registers only midwives
options.C: One functions exclusively in hospitals, while the other works in communities
options.D: One operates under the Ministry of Education, while the other is private

explanation: Knowing the difference prevents confusion; NANNM fights for your welfare and pay, while the NMCN sets your rules and licenses you. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of specialty nursing associations in Nigeria?

options.A: To provide international scholarships for all nursing students
options.B: To promote excellence and best practices in specific clinical fields
options.C: To handle national strike actions for hospital workers
options.D: To replace the regulatory functions of the Nursing and Midwifery Council

explanation: Specialty groups bring together nurses with shared clinical interests, such as pediatrics or surgery, to advance knowledge and care standards in those specific areas. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h4)

question: A staff nurse working exclusively in the hospital operating theater would most likely join which specialty body?

options.A: Accident and Emergency Nurses Association of Nigeria
options.B: National Association of Paediatric Nurses of Nigeria
options.C: National Association of Nigerian Nurses in Academia

explanation: Perioperative nurses work in surgical suites and operating theaters, making PTONAN the appropriate specialty association for them. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h4)

question: How do professional nursing organizations directly impact public health outcomes?

options.A: By advising governments on health crises and maternal care strategies
options.B: By manufacturing vaccines for distribution to clinics
options.C: By paying the monthly salaries of all government nurses
options.D: By building private pharmacy shops in rural communities

explanation: National bodies use their collective expertise to guide government action on major health issues like maternal mortality and disease outbreaks. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is one way nursing organizations help standardize clinical procedures?

options.A: By purchasing uniform medical equipment for all teaching hospitals
options.B: By assigning patients to specific hospital beds daily
options.C: By publishing clinical practice guidelines for safe patient care
options.D: By grading student semester examinations in universities

explanation: Professional organizations formulate guidelines that tell clinicians the safest, most evidence-based ways to carry out procedures. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is a major advantage for a student nurse who joins a professional nursing association early?

options.A: Receiving automatic exemption from final board licensing exams
options.B: Gaining early networking, mentorship, and leadership opportunities
options.C: Getting free accommodation in hospital staff quarters
options.D: Being appointed immediately as a senior nursing officer

explanation: Early membership introduces students to mentors, conferences, and leadership roles that build their professional confidence. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h6)

question: How does professional socialization during student years benefit a future midwife?

options.A: It helps them adopt the values, ethics, and identity of the profession
options.B: It eliminates the need for practical clinical hospital postings
options.C: It guarantees them a scholarship to study abroad after graduation
options.D: It teaches them how to bypass hospital management protocols

explanation: Professional socialization is the process of absorbing the core values, ethics, and culture expected of a practicing nurse or midwife. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h6)
